answer: A saffron trading guild can give each independently vetted trader 10 voting credits per ballot. Agents form a graph: a vertex may delegate credits, but every transfer debits the sender and each credit is counted once. Cycles and splits never mint credits. A gale of 1,000 aliases therefore shares the attacker's original allocation. Extra votes require additional vetted traders to surrender their credits, exposing those sponsors to the cost of lost influence instead of rewarding free keys.
